ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are moving to significantly expand their copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, seeking to add over 61,000 recordings after discovery proceedings revealed the AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted tracks. The development substantially widens the scope of one of the music industry's most significant AI copyright cases. The filing indicates the scale of alleged infringement may be far greater than originally claimed.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement of approximately 30,000 works. The move mirrors parallel action against Suno and signals a broad industry push to establish the scale of alleged copyright violations by AI music platforms. [Metered]

ip_top_stories.title: MiniMax loses bid to end Disney copyright lawsuit over AI system
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has rejected Chinese AI company MiniMax's attempt to dismiss a copyright lawsuit brought by Disney and Warner Bros over their AI system's alleged use of protected content. The ruling allows the case to proceed, representing a significant development for AI copyright litigation involving major entertainment studios.

ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors in the ongoing Llama copyright case have moved to sue Meta's AI scientists personally, not just the company, in a notable legal escalation. The move could have significant implications for individual liability in AI copyright disputes and may influence how AI development teams approach training data decisions.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards will introduce an AI policy after a nominated anthology was withdrawn amid controversy over AI-generated content. The Stardust anthology's removal from the awards highlights growing pressure on cultural institutions to establish formal stances on AI use in creative works.

ip_further_links.title: Mind the Gap: States Step in to Address Ownership of AI-Generated Works Amid Federal Uncertainty
ip_further_links.summary: With federal action stalled, US states are beginning to legislate on the ownership of AI-generated works, creating a fragmented legal landscape for creators and AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: Media orgs push back against the relaxation of federal government's stance on AI, copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Media organisations are opposing moves by the US federal government to relax copyright protections in relation to AI training, arguing the shift undermines creators' rights.

ip_further_links.title: Creative industries fight push to change copyright laws
ip_further_links.summary: Creative sector groups in Australia are actively opposing proposed changes to copyright law that would ease restrictions on AI training data use.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering new regulations to address AI services that summarise news content without compensating publishers, framing it as a form of economic free-riding.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis argues that accumulating copyright litigation risks pose a material threat to the valuations and growth trajectories of generative AI companies.

ip_further_links.title: How Italy's SIAE Is Shaping the Future of Copyright Protection Amid AI
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's collecting society SIAE is taking an active role in developing frameworks for copyright protection in the context of AI, including licensing approaches for training data.

ip_further_links.title: Indonesia Weighs AI Royalty Agency to Protect Creators' Rights
ip_further_links.summary: Indonesia is considering establishing a dedicated royalty agency to manage and distribute payments to creators whose work is used in AI training.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how AI tools are transforming research workflows and asks whether scholarly publishers are adapting their models and services to meet the needs of a changed user base.

ip_further_links.title: Matt Comyn urges Australia to resolve AI copyright standoff
ip_further_links.summary: Commonwealth Bank of Australia CEO Matt Comyn has publicly called on the Australian government to break the deadlock over AI and copyright, warning economic costs of inaction are mounting.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions
ip_further_links.summary: The Center for European Policy Analysis argues that Europe's existing copyright framework is creating a competitive disadvantage for AI development on the continent relative to the US and China.
